messages:
ashley: Heads-up — scheduling infra cutover for service-edge tonight 22:00 UTC. Deploy-bot will run a serial terraform apply for routing v2->v3 + IAM pin. Need manual ack on the IAM binding and a short release-note blurb. tagging @sam @leo @michelle

deploy-bot: Scheduled serial apply job 'svc-edge-cutover-2025-08-22' for 22:00 UTC. Will run in AZ order, backoff on failures. See runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/infra-cutover

sam: Hold — quick question: what's the rollback plan? last time an IAM pin caused auth failures across services. want explicit abort criteria.

leo: Canary plan I propose: 5% traffic -> monitor 15m -> 50% -> monitor 1h -> full. Traffic shift handled by gateway route weight. I'll run the smoke tests and post results.

michelle: IAM note: this adds a cross-account role binding for svc-account:service-edge-scaler. Security needs to OK the exact role ARN. @nate can you review the binding before we apply?

nate: Adding a short release-note now: "service-edge: routing upgrade + IAM pin for autoscaler; reduced cold-starts". I'll review the IAM role and push approval within ~30m.

ashley: I'll pin the provider and lock Terraform versions to avoid unexpected provider upgrades:
```hcl
terraform {
  required_providers {
    aws = {
      source = "hashicorp/aws"
      version = "= 4.59.0"
    }
  }
}
provider "aws" {
  version = "~> 4.59.0"
}
```
Also planning: state lock TTL = 15m, serial apply across AZs. Deploy-bot, please queue a dry-run plan now and hold for manual apply at 22:00.

sam: Please paste the trimmed terraform plan for only the IAM changes (so I can eyeball bindings). no full plan dump.

leo: IAM plan snippet (trimmed):
```
+ aws_iam_role.service_edge_scaler "service_edge_scaler"
+ aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.scaler_attach -> aws_iam_policy.scaler_policy
+ aws_iam_role_policy.service_edge_scaler_policy (new)
```
This matches the scoped binding we talked about.

deploy-bot: Dry-run executed: `terraform plan -target=module.iam -out=plan-dryrun`. No state changes outside IAM modules detected. Scheduled apply at 22:00 UTC.

oncall-bot: Note: monitoring threshold set — CPU spike alert at 80%. If CPU > 70% during canary window, the cutover will auto-abort.

michelle: Rollback criteria (formalized):
  1) auth error rate > 1% sustained over 5m
  2) p95 latency increase > 30% vs baseline over 10m
  3) infra CPU > 75% for > 10m
Rollback steps (short):
  - run: `deploy-bot rollback --to-tag v2-routing --reason "auth/latency regression"`
  - revert gateway weights to previous values
  - re-apply previous IAM state if needed (manual safe-apply)
  - open incident and tag #oncall + security
Runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/rollback-playbook

ashley: Quick rollback playbook snippet for ops:
```bash
# rollback to last healthy routing tag
deploy-bot rollback --to-version v2 --scope routing --wait-for-completion
# revert IAM (manual)
terraform apply -target=module.iam -var-file=rollback-vars.tfvars
```
I'll own the rollback actions if we need them.

nate: Approved the IAM binding with a note about least-privilege. Release note updated in the draft changelog.

leo: I'll post the smoke tests output in #eng-infra-smoke before 21:45. If tests pass, ready to proceed.

ashley: All acked? Summary: provider-pin + serial apply, manual IAM approval by @nate, rollback criteria set, release-note by @nate, smoke tests by @leo. If no objections by 21:30 UTC we execute canary at 22:00 UTC.

sam: Ack. I'll keep the pager and watch logs during the canary. good luck everyone :thumbsup:

ashley: Thanks — closing loop. I'll post apply start in this thread and ping ops-oncall when we begin.
